item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 220524
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
A tropical wave is forecast to move off the coast of western Africa
by Wednesday. Although environmental conditions are not expected to
be particularly conducive, some slow development of this system is
possible when it moves west-northwestward or northwestward across
the far eastern Atlantic. Interests in the Cabo Verde Islands
should monitor the progress of this system as gusty winds and areas
of heavy rain are possible there by the end of the week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
970 
WTNT31 KNHC 220840

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...FAY FORECAST TO BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE LATER TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM GMT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...31.8N 33.7W
ABOUT 570 MI...920 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 230 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1009 MB...29.80 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM GMT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 31.8 North, longitude 33.7 West. Fay is moving
toward the southwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A gradual turn toward the
west-southwest and then west is expected through midweek.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Fay is likely to degenerate into a post-tropical remnant low today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1009 mb (29.80 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 220841
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
Deep convection associated with Fay has completely dissipated, 
leaving the low-level center fully exposed on satellite imagery. 
Given the lack of organized deep convection over the past several 
hours, Fay's remaining time as a tropical cyclone is limited unless 
convection redevelops soon. Objective and subjective satellite 
intensity estimates currently range from 25 to 44 kt. Based on a 
blend of these estimates, the initial intensity is maintained at 35 
kt for this advisory.
 
The system is moving southwestward, or 230/8 kt, as it rounds the 
eastern periphery of a mid-level ridge to its west. A turn toward 
the west-southwest and then the west is expected over the next day 
or two, as the ridge strengthens. The latest NHC track forecast is 
near the previous nudged slightly towards the right, towards the 
GDMI and HCCA aids.
 
A combination of moderate wind shear and dry air entrainment should 
cause Fay to gradually spin down and weaken. Although shear may 
relax somewhat in a few days, as the system moves over slightly 
warmer sea surface temperatures, model-simulated satellite imagery 
suggests that any returning convection will occur only in 
intermittent bursts. Based on current trends and model guidance, the 
NHC intensity forecast calls for Fay to gradually weaken, and become 
a post-tropical remnant low later today and dissipate into an open 
trough by the end of the period.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
